## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Masked (single-blind) peer review — reviewer identities withheld from authors by default; author identities also withheld from reviewers, revealed to reviewers post-decision only upon author request/permission. Accepts both invited and unsolicited comprehensive review/meta-analysis submissions (no prior editorial invitation required to submit). |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | APA journals-wide (applies to Psychological Bulletin, no journal-specific override found): generative AI use in drafting must be disclosed in the Method/Introduction section and cited; AI cannot be named as an author; authors must verify all AI-provided content/citations; editors/reviewers are barred from entering manuscript text into generative AI tools (confidentiality). This is a publisher-level policy, not journal-specific, hence leniency scored as 3 (disclosure-gated, not a ban, not fully open) with signal_quality capped below 5 because no Psychological-Bulletin-specific AI statement was located separately from the APA-wide page. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/resources/publishing-tips/policy-generative-ai |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes. Psychological Bulletin accepts manuscripts that have previously appeared as preprints, working papers, white papers, or dissertations in publicly available online archives (e.g., PsyArXiv, ProQuest Dissertations & Theses). Authors must disclose this prior dissemination (2-4 sentences) in the author note at submission, per APA 7th-edition manuscript requirements.
> Source: https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/bul/index?tab=4

| Dimension | Assessment |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Meta-analyses and systematic/narrative research syntheses (quantitative or qualitative) across all subfields of scientific psychology; both invited and unsolicited comprehensive reviews are accepted (no editorial invitation required). Recent 2025-2026 published topics found: cross-temporal meta-analysis of perfectionism trends in Chinese college students (307 samples, Mar 2026), electronic screen use and children's socioemotional problems (systematic review + meta-analysis), reading anxiety and reading achievement (preregistered meta-analysis, 64 studies), trust and subjective well-being across the lifespan (multilevel meta-analysis), short-form video use and cognitive/mental health correlates (systematic review + meta-analysis).

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** meta-analysis, systematic review, narrative/qualitative research synthesis, expository/theoretical review grounded in prior evidence, preregistered meta-analysis

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **experiential.review_time_months**: SciRev shows 0 submitted reviews for Psychological Bulletin (all timing fields n/a); no Reddit r/AskAcademia thread found specifically discussing this journal's review time; 小木虫 (muchong.com) journal page contains only decade-old impact-factor numbers, no review-time reports; LetPub gives no numeric cycle, only 'undefined/variable' for invited pieces.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No source (SciRev, muchong, zhihu, fabiaoji, Reddit) reported any concrete desk-reject percentage or first-hand desk-reject anecdote for this specific journal.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No concrete first-hand forum post (中文 or English) describing reviewer tone/culture at Psychological Bulletin was found; only a generic 'very difficult to pass review' vendor-marketing characterization, which is not attributable to an identifiable reviewer/author account and was excluded as unreliable filler.
- **peer_review.type / preprint.allowed detail**: Not blank but noting these were sourced from a WebSearch AI-summarized aggregation of APA's Instructions to Authors content rather than a directly fetched primary page; recommend a follow-up WebFetch of https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/bul/index?tab=4 to confirm verbatim before publishing if higher confidence is needed.

**Cross-language checks performed (mandatory per methodology):**
- 小木虫 muchong.com (journal review/detail page jid=7036): only stale 2007-2009 impact-factor numbers posted by one user in 2010; 0 results for review-time or desk-reject discussion
- 知乎 zhihu.com: search surfaced general overview/ranking articles about Psychological Bulletin (e.g. zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/587565831) but no first-hand submission/review-experience threads; 0 experiential results
- fabiaoji.com / ifabiao.com (00332909 journal page): no concrete review-time, acceptance-rate, or desk-reject data; page is largely journal-metadata boilerplate
- LetPub (letpub.com.cn journalid=6998): vendor marketing page; only qualitative claim 'acceptance very difficult, invited-article cycle undefined' plus generic LetPub self-promotional stats (1.5x acceptance / 40% faster if using their editing service) — excluded as non-independent marketing claim, not a journal fact
- Reddit r/AskAcademia: web search (including site:reddit.com) returned 0 threads specifically discussing Psychological Bulletin submission/review experience
